..
Issued at 252 AM CST Mon Nov 2 2026

Early morning GOES water vapor imagery depicts a long-wave 
upper trough across the western CONUS. Weak mid-level ridging 
was noted downstream into the Mississippi Valley and western 
Great Lakes region. Latest surface map does indicate widespread 
low stratus just off to the south of the CWA across central 
IL/IN however, and this low-level moisture is expected to spread
north across the forecast area this morning as low level south-
southeast flow begins to strengthen downstream of the western 
trough. Have noted some minor (4-7SM) drops in visibility and 
some very weak clear-air VCP returns beneath stratus downstate, 
suggesting some patchy drizzle may be occurring, and this may 
spread north across our area this morning. Have continued to 
undercut NBM temperature guidance for today by roughly 3-5 
degrees (low-mid 60s) even with southeast winds becoming breezy,
given the expected extensive low-cloud cover. Model forecast 
soundings and time/height sections do indicate some increase in 
mid-level moisture later today with an approaching low-amplitude 
short wave currently over IA/MO, especially over northwest IL, 
where some scattered showers appear possible later this afternoon.

Tonight, a strong mid-level short wave currently heading into 
the central/southern Rockies is forecast to wrap northeastward 
across the Plains. Guidance remains in good agreement in 
depicting the development of a 45-50 kt low-level jet into the 
Midwest ahead of this feature, which will result in maintaining 
southerly surface winds that will likely result in steady or 
slowly rising temperatures overnight. The strongest forcing/ascent
continues to focus west of the Mississippi River overnight, 
though persistent warm advection/isentropic ascent is forecast 
to produce bands of showers from IA, across northwest IL into 
WI, mainly across the northwest third or so of the CWA.

Surface low pressure currently over far northeastern CO is 
forecast to lift northeast across eastern SD today and into MN 
this evening. A second area of low pressure associated with the 
strong Plains short wave is forecast to develop into the Kansas 
City vicinity by Tuesday morning, and eventually consolidate 
across MN/western WI by early Wednesday. During the course of 
this evolution, large scale forcing will gradually increase and 
result in increasing shower and possibly some thunderstorm 
coverage from west to east across the Illinois portion of the 
forecast area by Tuesday afternoon, especially west of the Fox 
Valley. Strong southerly winds, potentially gusting around 35 
mph at times, will work to boost temperatures across the area. 
Greater rain/shower coverage across our western CWA may limit 
warmth somewhat there, though low-mid 70s continue to look 
reasonable for afternoon highs farther east.
 
Tuesday evening/overnight continue to be the focus for the 
strongest large-scale forcing, including mid-level height falls, 
and increasing low/mid-level baroclinicity, and frontogenetic 
forcing ahead of the system's occluding cold front. Guidance 
continues to depict that an axis of heavier QPF in the vicinity
of the I-55/I-57 corridors may develop Tuesday night in 
association with a SSW-NNE oriented region of mid-level 
frontogenesis. This may support a period of steadier 
rain/embedded thunderstorms which could produce a localized 
corridor of heavier rainfall amounts. The occluding cold front 
is forecast to move across the area Wednesday morning, with 
shower coverage decreasing and becoming more scattered behind 
the front. Temperatures will be cooler Wednesday, though still 
above average for early November with expected highs in the low-
mid 60s. Southwest winds will likely remain gusty, potentially 
still 30-35 mph.

Models continue to show some spread by the end of the week with
how quickly the system departs, with the GEFS faster and the 
CMCE slowest. Eventually however, weak surface high pressure is 
expected to develop by late Friday/Saturday, with a cool-down to
slightly below average temperatures (50s by day, 30s at night).
There is a signal in all of the global guidance for another 
northwest-flow short wave to dig into the western Lakes region 
toward Sunday, which may support additional shower chances.

Ratzer
